topics.title: Admin overview
topics.summary: Understand the dedicated Admin host, organization context, dashboard, and access boundary.
prerequisites: Required access: System Administrator or Organization Administrator.
steps: Use the dedicated Admin URL supplied by your deployment administrator.
Sign in with a verified, active account.
Confirm the active organization before making changes.
topics.result: The dashboard loads only the workspaces allowed by your effective role.
failures: A non-admin account is sent to Access denied.
An expired or revoked session returns to login.
topics.audit: Authentication success and failure events are audited.
notes: Use the dedicated Admin host: admin.powerdoxautomation.com for PXA Cloud or admin.{customer-host} for a customer deployment.
The browser calls the API through same-origin /api; PXA.Company intentionally does not expose an Admin navigation link.
The active organization controls tenant-scoped lists and mutations.

topics.title: Users and invitations
topics.summary: Invite users, search memberships, edit profiles, change status, and run safe bulk actions.
steps: Open Users and select Invite user.
Enter display name, email, and organization roles.
Send the invitation and wait for email verification.
Open the user detail page to manage status, seats, sessions, or password reset.
topics.result: The user receives a single-use invitation and appears in the organization membership list.
failures: Duplicate invitations return a generic conflict.
Self-deactivation and removal of the last administrator are blocked.
topics.audit: Invitation, profile, status, role, seat, session, and bulk actions create actor-attributed audit events.
notes: Deactivation blocks access and revokes sessions; soft deletion also removes the organization membership while retaining audit history.
Restoration reactivates the retained membership but does not silently restore old sessions.
Bulk actions report protected or rejected users instead of partially hiding failures.

topics.title: Organizations
topics.permission: Organization Administrator; System Administrator for cross-tenant work
topics.summary: Create and maintain organizations, memberships, status, and active tenant context.
prerequisites: Required access: Organization Administrator; System Administrator for cross-tenant work.
steps: Open Organizations.
Select an organization or create one if you are a System Administrator.
Edit its name or status.
Attach existing users or remove memberships.
Use Switch organization before managing another tenant.
topics.result: All subsequent Admin queries are scoped to the selected organization.
failures: Organization Administrators cannot browse other tenants.
Self-removal and last-administrator removal are rejected.
topics.audit: Creation, updates, membership changes, and tenant selection are audited.
notes: System Administrators can create organizations and work across tenants; Organization Administrators remain tenant-scoped.
Switching the active organization refreshes authorization context and invalidates stale workspace assumptions.
The final active Organization Administrator cannot remove or demote themselves.

topics.title: Roles and permissions
topics.summary: Assign protected organization roles while keeping product access separate.
steps: Open Roles & permissions.
Inspect the permission matrix.
Open Manager, Editor, Viewer, or Organization Administrator.
Assign or revoke the role for an active membership.
topics.result: The affected user receives updated organization permissions after session refresh.
failures: System Administrator is never assignable through tenant role APIs.
Self-role changes and removal of the last administrator are blocked.
topics.audit: Every assignment and revocation records actor, role, target user, tenant, and outcome.
notes: System Administrator is an operator role and is never assignable from an organization role screen.
Organization roles grant permissions; product entitlements and seat assignments are evaluated independently.
Role changes revoke stale sessions so refreshed claims become authoritative.

topics.title: Subscriptions and entitlements
topics.permission: System Administrator for mutations; Organization Administrator for read access
topics.summary: Manage edition, lifecycle, seats, usage, and product entitlements without confusing them with roles.
prerequisites: Required access: System Administrator for mutations; Organization Administrator for read access.
steps: Open Subscriptions and select an organization.
Review edition, lifecycle dates, deployment, and seat limit.
Apply an approved lifecycle action.
Edit capability grants and limits.
Assign seats to active memberships.
Review usage and lifecycle history.
topics.result: The subscription policy immediately exposes the new effective entitlements to protected product operations.
failures: Unsupported lifecycle transitions are rejected.
A role never grants a missing product entitlement.
Seat limits and inactive memberships block assignment.
topics.audit: Subscription, entitlement, lifecycle, and seat mutations are audited and added to lifecycle history.
notes: Edition, lifecycle state, account type, deployment mode, seats, and entitlements are separate subscription properties.
Trial extension, renewal, grace period, cancellation, suspension, and expiry use validated lifecycle transitions.
Usage is read-only evidence and does not itself grant an entitlement.

topics.title: Offline licenses
topics.summary: Issue, validate, download, and revoke signed Enterprise licenses for approved deployments.
steps: Open Offline licenses.
Select an eligible Enterprise subscription.
Enter product version, deployment ID, validity, and instance limit.
Issue and download the signed artifact.
Validate before delivery and revoke when required.
topics.result: A signed license contains the approved products and limits without exposing the private signing key.
failures: Non-Enterprise subscriptions are ineligible.
Tampered, expired, mismatched, or revoked licenses fail validation.
topics.audit: Issuance, validation-sensitive changes, download context, and revocation are auditable.
notes: Only approved Enterprise On-Premise or Hybrid subscriptions can receive an offline license.
Replacement means issuing a new signed artifact and revoking the superseded license; private signing keys never enter Admin.
Expired, revoked, deployment-mismatched, or tampered artifacts fail validation.

topics.title: Service accounts and API keys
topics.summary: Create non-human identities and short-lived or revocable API credentials for automation.
steps: Open Service accounts.
Create an account with an explicit name and expiry.
Create an API key.
Store the secret immediately because it is shown once.
Revoke keys or the service account when access changes.
topics.result: SDK and automation calls can authenticate without receiving Admin permissions.
failures: A lost secret cannot be displayed again; create a replacement.
Expired or revoked credentials are rejected immediately.
topics.audit: Service-account creation, key creation, use metadata, and revocation are audited without storing raw secrets.
notes: A service account is a non-human organization identity; an API key is one revocable credential owned by that identity.
The raw key is displayed exactly once. PXA stores only the protected verification material and a non-secret prefix.
Rotation creates a replacement key, updates the consumer, verifies it, and then revokes the old key.

topics.title: Mail delivery
topics.summary: Inspect transactional mail state and safely retry or cancel queued messages.
steps: Open Mail delivery.
Filter by state, template, or recipient-safe metadata.
Inspect attempts and sanitized failure reason.
Retry a recoverable failure or cancel a pending message after confirmation.
topics.result: The queue records the next delivery state without exposing protected payloads or action tokens.
failures: Permanent failures move to dead letter.
Disabled transports retain a truthful non-delivered state.
Delivered messages cannot be resent accidentally.
topics.audit: Retry and cancellation actions are audited; message bodies and tokens are never placed in audit details.
notes: The workspace exposes sanitized delivery metadata, never message bodies, reset links, invitation tokens, or provider credentials.
Retry is limited to failed or dead-letter messages; cancellation is limited to undelivered terminal-safe states.
Marketing consent does not control transactional security delivery.

topics.title: Audit workspace
topics.permission: Organization Administrator; Enterprise required for export
topics.summary: Search immutable privileged activity and export a tenant-scoped evidence set.
prerequisites: Required access: Organization Administrator; Enterprise required for export.
steps: Open Audit.
Filter by action, target, outcome, actor, or time range.
Open an event to inspect structured details.
Export the filtered result as CSV or JSON when entitled.
topics.result: Results remain limited to the active organization and preserve stable action keys.
failures: Malformed historical details appear as unavailable.
Exports are limited to 50,000 rows.
Spreadsheet formula prefixes are neutralized.
topics.audit: Successful audit exports create their own audit event; audit records cannot be edited.
notes: Audit results and exports are always scoped to the active tenant unless explicit system authorization applies.
CSV exports neutralize spreadsheet-formula prefixes and are capped at 50,000 rows.
Retention is deployment policy; immutable records cannot be edited from Admin.

topics.title: System status and telemetry
topics.summary: Inspect sanitized service health and open protected metrics, logs, and traces without exposing operator telemetry to organization administrators.
prerequisites: Use an active, email-verified System Administrator account.
Use the Admin and operator hosts configured for the same deployment.
Confirm that the optional observability profile is healthy.
steps: Open System status in PXA.Admin and review the coarse component and queue states.
Select Open dashboards to enter the protected operator gateway.
Use Platform Overview first, then open the infrastructure, operations, document, or browser dashboard for the affected surface.
Use Grafana Explore only when dashboard evidence requires a correlated metric, sanitized log, or Tempo trace.
Record the UTC time, dashboard, alert name, runbook ID, and W3C trace ID when escalating.
topics.result: Authorized system operators can correlate sanitized platform health, metrics, logs, traces, and alerts while customer administrators see no raw telemetry.
failures: Anonymous access receives 401 and Organization Administrators receive 403 from the operator gateway.
A healthy Admin status page does not replace liveness, readiness, or alert evidence.
Mailpit, Collector health, and container health URLs are local evaluation endpoints and must not be exposed publicly.
topics.audit: Opening telemetry is a protected read. Remediation performed through Admin or deployment tooling remains separately auditable.
notes: PXA.Admin exposes only sanitized status. Raw Grafana data remains behind the System Administrator operator gateway.
Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Alertmanager, cAdvisor, and PostgreSQL Exporter have no direct public host ports.
Use local links only for Rancher Desktop evaluation. Production links require TLS and the deployment operator allowlist.
Never paste customer documents, credentials, mail payloads, license material, or arbitrary query attributes into telemetry tools.

topics.title: Settings and common states
topics.summary: Recognize loading, empty, forbidden, offline, stale, failure, and confirmation states.
steps: Check the active organization and connection state.
Retry transient API failures.
Refresh stale data after reconnecting.
Use the request trace ID when escalating a persistent failure.
topics.result: The UI preserves already loaded data as stale instead of presenting it as current.
failures: Forbidden means the effective role lacks permission.
Unavailable means the API capability is not deployed.
Offline means no mutation should be assumed successful.
topics.audit: No audit event is created when a rejected request does not change state.
notes: Loading has no prior value; stale preserves a prior value after a connectivity loss; empty is a successful query with no records.
Forbidden is an authorization result, while unavailable indicates a missing or disabled server capability.
Destructive operations always require explicit confirmation and a truthful final result.

topics.title: Security model
topics.summary: Understand sessions, CSRF, tenant isolation, and the difference between roles and entitlements.
prerequisites: Required access: Application integrator or administrator.
steps: Use the host-only HttpOnly Admin session cookie.
Send the CSRF header on every browser mutation.
Resolve organization context from authenticated claims.
Treat server authorization as authoritative.
topics.result: Browser, API-key, tenant, and product-access boundaries remain independent and auditable.
failures: Hidden navigation is not authorization.
API keys do not grant Admin permissions.
Changing role or status revokes stale sessions.
topics.audit: Authentication, authorization-sensitive changes, and session revocation produce security audit events.
notes: Admin uses a host-only HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookie. Do not introduce a parent-domain authentication cookie.
Browser mutations require a fresh CSRF token and X-PXA-CSRF header; API keys are for service clients, not Admin browser elevation.
The server resolves organization context from the authenticated session and never trusts a tenant ID in a request body.

topics.title: Admin API and diagnostics
topics.summary: Use the versioned Admin API, standard pagination, Problem Details, and stable diagnostics.
steps: Authenticate through the Admin session.
Fetch a CSRF token before a mutation.
Call routes under /api/pxa/v1/admin.
Handle application/problem+json and retain the trace identifier.
topics.result: Clients receive bounded tenant-scoped data and stable error contracts.
failures: PXAAPI001-008 distinguish validation, authentication, authorization, CSRF, conflict, rate limit, unavailable, and internal failures.
Never log cookies, raw API keys, reset tokens, or mail payloads.
topics.audit: Every successful privileged mutation declares and persists its expected audit action.
notes: Public Admin operations use /api/pxa/v1/admin and bounded pagination. OpenAPI is available from the deployment API reference.
Problem Details diagnostics remain stable: PXAAPI001 validation, 002 authentication, 003 authorization, 004 CSRF, 005 conflict, 006 rate limit, 007 unavailable, and 008 internal failure.
Retain the diagnostic code and trace ID for support, but never log cookies, raw keys, tokens, or customer document data.

topics.title: Troubleshooting and support
topics.summary: Diagnose access, tenant, mail, subscription, license, and stale-session problems safely.
steps: Record the timestamp, route, active organization, diagnostic code, and trace ID.
Confirm account, membership, subscription, and session status.
Retry only operations documented as idempotent.
Escalate without attaching secrets or customer documents.
topics.result: Support receives enough metadata to correlate logs without receiving credentials or protected content.
failures: Repeated 401 indicates an invalid session.
403 indicates missing permission or operator authorization.
409 indicates a protected business or concurrency rule.
429 requires waiting for the retry window.
topics.audit: Troubleshooting reads do not create mutation events; corrective privileged actions do.
notes: Capture the UTC time, route, active organization name, diagnostic code, and trace ID before escalation.
Do not send screenshots containing unmasked email addresses, IDs, API keys, tokens, license artifacts, or customer data.
Emergency access and platform recovery belong to the protected operator publication, not this public site.
